title: Fill a Van With the Most Items
statement:
A delivery van can carry at most capacity boxes. The warehouse has several kinds of boxes: boxKinds[i] = [count, itemsPerBox] means there are count boxes of kind i, and each of them holds itemsPerBox items.

Load any boxes you like, up to capacity boxes in total. Return the largest total number of items the van can carry. If there are fewer boxes than capacity, you can simply load them all.

examples.why: Take all four boxes of 9 items (36), then one box of 5 items. Ranking kinds by how many boxes they have would pick a 1-item box next and reach only 37.
Only three boxes exist, so all of them go in: 3 + 2 + 2.

hints: Every box takes the same single slot in the van. So which boxes deserve the slots first?
A box with more items is always at least as good as a box with fewer. The number of boxes of a kind does not matter for that choice.
Sort the kinds by itemsPerBox, largest first. Take as many as fit from each kind until the van is full.

explain.intuition:
All boxes cost the same: one slot. So the best plan simply fills slots with the fullest boxes first. If some slot held a box with fewer items while a fuller box was left behind, swapping them would only increase the total. That swap argument is the whole proof of the greedy.

Sort the kinds by items per box, descending, and take min(count, slotsLeft) boxes of each. Because itemsPerBox is at most 1000, you can even skip the sort and bucket the counts by items per box, like a counting sort.
steps: For each kind, take t = min(count, left) boxes: add t · itemsPerBox to total and subtract t from left.
pitfalls: Sorting by count or by count · itemsPerBox. The slot cost is per box, so only items per box matters.
Taking a whole kind even when it does not fit, overshooting capacity.
Looping one box at a time when capacity is a million: it works but is needlessly slow. Take a whole batch with min.

complexity.time: O(k log k) with sorting, O(k + 1000) with buckets

solutions.title: Sort by items per box
solutions.idea: Fill the van with the fullest boxes first, taking as many of each kind as still fit.

solutions.title: Buckets by items per box
solutions.idea: itemsPerBox is at most 1000, so add up box counts per items-per-box value and walk the buckets from 1000 down.

followups: Boxes now also have different sizes and the van has a volume limit instead of a box limit. Does the greedy still work?
The warehouse streams in new box kinds and you must answer after each one. What would you keep to avoid re-sorting?
